haiku-low.q1: None visible. Both get 401 with the same "Invalid email or password" body and no other header or content difference. Unknown emails run a bcrypt compare against a dummy hash to match timing.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 "Too many failed attempts. Try again later." The password is not checked and no failure is recorded. The lock lasts until 15 minutes after the newest failure.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session row is deleted, whether valid or not, in the same transaction that inserts the new session, so there is never both or neither.
haiku-low.q4: The cookie 'sid' carries a raw 32-byte base64url random token. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. The server stores only its SHA-256 hash.
haiku-low.q5: It stops 12 hours after creation, the absolute cap, since it never moves. The 30-minute idle timeout restarts on each request but cannot extend past that cap.
haiku-low.q6: It returns zero rows, deletes the expired row best-effort, and responds 302 to /login while clearing the cookie.
haiku-low.q7: If a cookie is present, the server deletes the session row by hash, logging and continuing on storage error. Then it returns 302 to /login with the cookie cleared. With no session, the delete is skipped and the response is identical.
haiku-low.q8: Sessions are stored in a Postgres sessions table. Any app instance finds one by looking up the SHA-256 hash of the cookie value in the shared database.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt, keyed by lowercase email with failed_at. The server reads the newest 5 rows from the last 25 minutes and compares timestamps: 5 within 10 minutes locks.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that now() is before expires_at and that now() minus last_seen_at is under 30 minutes. If valid, it writes back last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id, in one UPDATE statement.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 response with the generic "Something went wrong, please try again" page. The transaction rolls back, so no new session is created, the old session row remains, and failure rows are not cleared.
haiku-low.q12: A 15-minute sweep timer on every instance deletes expired or idle sessions. Failed lookups also lazily delete expired rows. Correctness does not depend on this cleanup.

sonnet.q1: It does not differ. Both get 401 re-showing the login page with "Invalid email or password", same body, same headers and content. The unknown email also runs a dummy bcrypt compare so timing matches.
sonnet.q2: It is locked out: the server returns 429 (login page, "Too many failed attempts. Try again later.", no countdown) without checking the password. No new failure row is recorded. This holds while now is under 15 minutes after the newest failure.
sonnet.q3: On successful login the old session row is deleted (valid or not) and a new session with a new ID is inserted, in the same transaction. This prevents session fixation.
sonnet.q4: The cookie (sid) carries only the raw random token (32 bytes CSPRNG, base64url), with no expiry. Page scripts cannot read it because it is HttpOnly (also Secure, SameSite=Lax, host-only).
sonnet.q5: At the 12-hour absolute cap from creation (expires_at), even with continuous activity, because the idle timeout of 30 minutes keeps renewing but the cap never moves.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns zero rows. The app tries a best-effort DELETE of the row if it is expired (errors logged and ignored), then responds 302 to /login and clears the cookie.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, the server deletes the session row by hash (on storage error it logs and continues). Then it responds 302 to /login and clears the cookie. If no session or cookie, the DELETE is skipped and the response is identical.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table (id = SHA-256 hash of the cookie token). Both instances share the database, so any instance hashes the cookie value and looks up that row; no sticky routing or Redis needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row per failed attempt keyed by lowercase submitted email with failed_at. The server reads the newest 5 rows for that email from the last 25 minutes and checks that the newest and 5th-newest are at most 10 minutes apart (and now is before newest plus 15 minutes).
sonnet.q10: It compares now() (database clock) against expires_at (must be later) and against last_seen_at (must be within 30 minutes), in a single UPDATE statement. When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 with a generic "Something went wrong, please try again" page. The transaction rolls back, no new session is created, the old session row stays, and failure rows are not cleared.
sonnet.q12: The sweep: every instance runs a timer at startup and every 15 minutes, deleting sessions where expires_at has passed or last_seen_at is over 30 minutes old. Also the lazy delete when an expired session is presented (best effort).
